subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Wi-Fi: Wireless Local Networks
description: A fast breakdown of Wi-Fi: Wireless Local Networks for builders.

hook.text: Wi-Fi uses unlicensed radio bands to create wireless local area networks — no cables, no licenses.

buildup.text: The 2.4 GHz band penetrates walls well but is crowded. The 5 GHz band is faster but shorter range.

discovery.text: CSMA/CA: before transmitting, a device listens for silence on the channel to avoid collisions.

twist.text: Wi-Fi 6 introduced OFDMA — letting the access point serve multiple devices simultaneously per channel.

climax.text: Wi-Fi 7 uses 320 MHz channels and 4096-QAM for speeds exceeding 40 Gbps in theory.

punchline.text: Unlicensed spectrum, smart protocols — Wi-Fi made wireless networking universal.

quiz.question: What does CSMA/CA do before a Wi-Fi device transmits?
options: It boosts the signal power to maximum
It listens for channel silence to avoid colliding with other transmissions
It switches to a different frequency band automatically
